TL-Drum5.notes: The parameter indices do not follow the panel: the enum interleaves the five voices (PUSH_KK is 0, LINK_KK 1, LINK_OH 2, PUSH_CH 3 and so on), so tagging from index order would attach every line to the wrong voice. The panel order left to right is snare, open hat, kick, closed hat, clap, and the tags here follow the census x positions. The manual says Push "boosts the signal level 50%"; applyBoost in helpers/dsp_utils.hpp:198 multiplies by 1.5 and then clamps to ±1 before the volume stage, so a loud sample is clipped rather than made louder. Decay times of 80ms to 800ms come from DecayEnvelope in helpers/dsp_utils.hpp:113-122; the manual gives no figures. Panning is applied only to the stereo mix, never to the individual outputs. Every jack is read with getVoltage(), so nothing is polyphonic.

A rising edge past 1V moves the lower sequencer on one step, or back one step while its reverse switch is on.
Chooses 8 or 16 steps for the lower sequencer.
Reverses the direction the lower sequencer runs in.

Note — There is no reset jack. Reset arrives only from a TL_Reseter placed directly to the left or the right, whose A half resets the upper sequencer and B half the lower one.
Note — A reset puts the playhead at the first step, or at the last step while that sequencer is reversed.
Note — Shortening a sequencer does not move the playhead. If it was on a step beyond the new length it stays there until the next clock brings it back inside.

TL_Seq4.notes: The eight step latches of the upper sequencer share one line and the sixteen of the lower share another: within a sequencer they differ only by step number. The CV Steps and CV Reverse inputs write their result back into the panel parameter every sample, so those two switches cannot be moved by hand while a cable is toggling them faster than you can click. The clock input is a level compare at 1V feeding a Schmitt trigger on the resulting boolean, so an input that never falls below 1V never clocks again. Nothing in this plugin saves module state to the patch; only parameter positions come back. Every jack is read with getVoltage(), so nothing is polyphonic.

TL_Mixes.notes: The maker's summary calls this a 7-channel stereo mixer with cutoff; the CUT control is a switch, not a sweep, and puts in a fixed 180Hz first-order high-pass (cutHz at TL_Mixes.cpp:60). The VOL CV multiplies the knob rather than adding to it, so the knob sets a ceiling and the jack sets how much of it is used; with the knob at zero the CV can do nothing. The pan CV replaces the knob outright while patched. On a channel with both inputs connected the pan acts as a balance that attenuates one side, while a channel with only one input connected is panned equal-power across both. The VOL knobs and the MASTER slider both default to zero, which is unusual and makes a fresh module silent. Every jack is read with getVoltage(), so nothing is polyphonic. The seven channels are identical in behaviour and share one line per control; their parameter and port indices do run left to right across the panel.

TL_Shape.notes: The envelope and the VCA are independent: processVca() reads only CV In and the VOL knob, never env (TL_Shape.cpp:166-196). The maker's summary calls the module "ADSR + VCA" without saying the two are not joined internally, which is the thing most likely to make it look broken. The gate test is a level compare at 1V rather than a Schmitt trigger, and the panel TRIG button is a gate rather than a trigger: it holds the envelope at sustain while held. The release always falls from whatever level the envelope had reached, over the full release time. Times run from 1ms to 10 seconds (knobToTime at TL_Shape.cpp:94); the maker gives no figures. Every jack is read with getVoltage(), so nothing is polyphonic.
